title: An equivalent integer lattice basis uses integer coefficients and determinant ±1
summary: When using rows as a basis, left multiplication by an integer invertible matrix U with det U=±1 can preserve the generated integer lattice.
applies: Integer lattice; convention for row vectors as bases
detail: Add one row to an integer multiple of another row to get the same grid. Multiplying a row by 2 usually results in only the cells of the original cell.
boundary: The two bases span the same real vector space and cannot be derived to generate the same integer grid.
relevance: Verify whether the lattice basis reduction output only changes a set of basis, rather than changing the set of candidate points.
